legend: An unordered pair of natural numbers is called good if one of the numbers divides the other. Output n%%ZSMJ0%% such natural numbers not exceeding one million, such that there are exactly k%%ZSMJ1%% good pairs among them, or determine that this is impossible.

More formally: for the numbers output by your program a1%%ZSMJ2%%, a2%%ZSMJ3%%, ..., an%%ZSMJ4%%, there must be exactly k%%ZSMJ5%% pairs of indices i%%ZSMJ6%%, j%%ZSMJ7%%, where i<j%%ZSMJ8%%, such that ai%%ZSMJ9%% divides aj%%ZSMJ10%% or aj%%ZSMJ11%% divides ai%%ZSMJ12%%.
input: Two integers n%%ZSMJ13%% and k%%ZSMJ14%% are given, each on a separate line (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ15%%, 0≤k≤105%%ZSMJ16%%).
output: Output n%%ZSMJ17%% such natural numbers in the range from 1 to 106%%ZSMJ18%%, such that there are exactly k%%ZSMJ19%% good pairs among them. If there are multiple correct answers, output any. If there are no solutions, output -1.
Subtask 3 (up to 40 points): no additional constraints.
